key_insight: Instead of increasing channel width to preserve reconstruction at low bitrates, TC-AE reallocates representational capacity into the token dimension of a ViT-style latent space, preventing latent collapse and preserving generative quality under deep compression.
problem_solved: Deep compression autoencoders that boost channel count to maintain quality often cause latent representation collapse and degraded generative performance at high compression ratios; TC-AE addresses this by changing how capacity is organized in the latent space.
method: ViT-based autoencoder that emphasizes token-level latent capacity over raw channel expansion, i.e., increasing and structuring tokens rather than just channels.

Token-centric design and lightweight architectural changes (tokenization, attention-informed aggregation/expansion) to preserve diversity and avoid collapse without multi-stage training or heavy channel growth.
Compatibility-focused approach: simple modifications that integrate with existing codecs and training pipelines to improve reconstruction and generative fidelity at low bitrates.
impact: TC-AE enables better image reconstruction and generative quality at aggressive compression rates while avoiding the instability of oversized channel latents—useful for storage- and bandwidth-constrained ML systems and downstream generative tasks.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram comparing conventional channel-heavy latent autoencoder vs TC-AE's token-centric ViT latent pipeline

paper_title: TC-AE: Unlocking Token Capacity for Deep Compression Autoencoders
paper_authors: Teng Li, Ziyuan Huang, Cong Chen, Yangfu Li, Yuanhuiyi Lyu
